payload.headline: AMD: fast growth and rising margins, but the price runs far past value

summary.thesis: AMD's business is getting stronger fast, but at 552.9 the price already assumes years of growth well beyond what any of our valuation methods support.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait, with no new buying at these levels. Swing: wait, because the price sits in the middle of its range just under resistance.
summary.act_at: Revisit near 480.33–502.6 support; value case only near 333.38 or below

payload.happening: AMD closed at 552.9. It traded at 576.7 intraday (as of 10:54 ET, not a close), up 7.32% on the day, which takes it into the 574.2–596.07 resistance zone. There is no news in our data since the last note. The next earnings report is on 2027-02-02.
payload.business: Business facts: demand is speeding up. Sales grew 44.68% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, compared with 37.85% two quarters ago. Trailing revenue is 45.4B, up from 32.0B. Profitability is improving too. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 17.72% from 8.78%, and free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) rose to 7.1B from 5.4B. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash is 8.7B and liquidity is 15.8B. Analysts are raising their numbers: next-year EPS (earnings per share) estimates are up 12.1% in 30 days. What is at risk: inventory grew 57% while quarterly sales grew 45%. Unsold product can lead to price cuts. And the 17.72% operating margin sits near the top of its 5-year range of -2% to 22%, a level that often fades. Dilution is modest at 1.22% a year, and stock pay (SBC) is 4.4% of revenue. Today's 7.32% jump has no news behind it in our data, so it changes sentiment, not the business.

worth.text: At 552.9 the price is above every valuation method we have. Our discounted cash flow model (DCF: today's value of future cash) gives 148.51 / 190.99 / 226.75 for bear / base / bull. The model caps starting growth at 30%. Even at that cap the value is 190.99, and at 20% growth it is 132.38. Pricing AMD by its own past price-to-sales gives 179.24–333.38. The stock trades at 20.0 times sales, compared with a peer median of 14.7, and sits at the 93rd percentile of its own 5-year range. The gap comes down to one input: the DCF caps growth at 30%, but analysts expect next-year EPS growth of 119%. If that happens, next year's P/E (price divided by earnings) is 31.3, far below today's trailing 120.5. Margins matter too. If operating margin fell to 13%, the model value would drop to 100.61.
worth.key_assumption: The price only makes sense if analysts' forecast of a jump to 17.69 EPS next year comes true and earnings keep growing beyond the 30% the model allows.

bull: Growth is speeding up: quarterly sales grew 44.68% from a year earlier, compared with 37.85% two quarters ago.
Margins nearly doubled: operating margin rose to 17.72% from 8.78%, and free cash flow reached 7.1B.
Analysts keep raising forecasts: next-year EPS of 17.69 is up 12.1% in 30 days, which would bring the forward P/E down to 31.3.
bear: Valuation is stretched: the price of 552.9 is above the full fair-value range of 148.51–333.38, and the trailing P/E is 120.5.
Inventory rose 57% while sales rose 45%, a possible early sign of future price cuts.
Operating margin of 17.72% is near its 5-year peak of 22%. If it fell to 13%, the model value would drop to 100.61.

levels.what: Last close. It is above every valuation method, so it is not a level to buy at.
Top of the 480.33–502.6 support zone (5 touches). This is a better entry if the business keeps beating expectations.
Top of the fair-value range (own-history price-to-sales high). This is where the valuation case begins.

longterm.why: This is a strong, improving business at a price that leaves little room for disappointment. The fair-value top of 333.38 is far below the price, so waiting costs little.

swing.why: The trend is a range, and the price sits at its 50-day average of 550.43. Today's intraday push runs straight into the 574.2–596.07 resistance zone. A setup would be a pullback that holds the 517.35–530.13 support zone, or a close above 596.07.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-02-02 are not close yet, but options imply a 15.6% move by 2026-12-18. The report against the 2.93 EPS and 17.1B revenue consensus is the next real test.

change_mind: A close above 596.07 with next-year EPS estimates still rising above 17.69 would show the market backing the growth case, which argues for a more constructive stance.
A close below 480.33, the bottom of the lower support zone, would break the range and argue for avoiding the stock.
If the 2027-02-02 report shows operating margin slipping from 17.72% toward 13%, or inventory growth still running ahead of sales, the bear case would win.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
